trigger: Hypothesized: rbac_enforcement_in_effect and check_permission are two separate decision points in response_visible_set_fn that 'must agree' on a degrade, and a narrow timing window between them could let global_read spuriously resolve true, granting nullopt (fleet-wide view) to a caller who should be scope-limited.
refuted_by: rbac_store.cpp:1608-1625 (rbac_enforcement_in_effect fails closed on a degraded view, comment: 'Treat a degraded view... the same as enabled') and rbac_store.cpp:2536-2588 (check_permission returns false on !open_, breaker-open, and pool-acquire-timeout -- every degrade path returns false, never true)
refuted_by_reporter: orchestrator (governance-agent, independent of unhappy-path's reporting agent and of the branch's author)
summary: REFUTED by the orchestrator via direct code reading (not the reporting agent, not the branch author): rbac_enforcement_in_effect (rbac_store.cpp:1608) deliberately treats a degraded/stale RBAC-enabled view the SAME as 'enabled' (fails closed, returns true -- enforcement stays in effect); check_permission (rbac_store.cpp:2536) fails closed (returns false) on every degrade path (!open_, breaker-open, pool-acquire-timeout). global_read can therefore never be spuriously true on a degrade; the resolver always falls through correctly to the fail-closed visible_agents_for_permission branch. This is the SAME hardened, extensively-tested (#2703) primitive used by every other confinement-critical caller in the codebase, not a new/fragile decision point this branch introduces.
rationale: Security-control-behavior claim; security-guardian's lane, refuted by the orchestrator acting in a governance-agent capacity independent of the unhappy-path reporter and the branch author.
